name: Toyota GR86
notes: Toyota GR86 (2022+), 2.4L NA flat-4, 6MT. 228 hp crank, curb weight 1275 kg. Cd 0.29 x ~2.0 m2 frontal area. Performance summer tyres. ~140 mph claimed top speed. Line quality (driving-line precision, a driver/chassis trait like aggression — not a published spec) set high for a light, communicative RWD sports car. Naturally aspirated (R9): loses power with altitude in proportion to air density, unlike this roster's turbo/hybrid/electric cars. Peak-power road speed (R14, a hand-waved per-gear approximation, not a real spec) set moderate-high for a revvy NA flat-4.

name: VW Golf GTI
notes: Volkswagen Golf GTI Mk8 (2022+), 2.0L turbo, DSG. 241 hp crank. Cd 0.30 x ~2.2 m2. 155 mph, electronically limited. Line quality set at the roster default — a capable but not razor-precise FWD hot hatch. Peak-power road speed set low — a torquey turbo four makes its power low in the rev range.

name: Toyota Camry
notes: Toyota Camry (2018-2023), 2.5L NA I4. 203 hp crank. Cd 0.27 x ~2.3 m2. Standard touring tyres. ~135 mph typical family-sedan governed estimate. Line quality set low — a comfort-oriented family sedan, not driven for cornering precision. Naturally aspirated (R9): loses power with altitude in proportion to air density, unlike this roster's turbo/hybrid/electric cars. Peak-power road speed set at the roster-typical default for an unremarkable NA four.

name: Honda Civic Type R
notes: Honda Civic Type R FL5 (2023+), 2.0L turbo, 6MT. 315 hp crank. Cd ~0.33 (wing/aero kit) x ~2.2 m2. High-performance summer tyres. Manufacturer-claimed 171 mph. Fastest small car here, and by far the likeliest to crash. Line quality set high — a track-focused FWD chassis with sharp turn-in despite the drivetrain layout. Peak-power road speed set moderate — turbocharged but tuned to rev cleanly.

name: Toyota RAV4
notes: Toyota RAV4 (2023), 2.5L NA I4. 203 hp crank. Cd 0.34 x ~2.6 m2. Crossover all-season tyres. Top speed is an estimate, not a marketed spec for this class. Overconfident in a tall, lower-grip vehicle. Line quality set at the floor (1.0, no widening) — a tall crossover with no precision-driving pretensions. Naturally aspirated (R9): loses power with altitude in proportion to air density, unlike this roster's turbo/hybrid/electric cars. Peak-power road speed set near the roster default — an unremarkable NA four.

name: Ford F-150
notes: Ford F-150 SuperCrew 4x2 (2023), 2.7L EcoBoost V6. 325 hp crank. Cd ~0.43 x ~3.25 m2 - full-size pickup. Truck-rated tyres, heavier vehicle. ~100 mph typical electronic speed limiter for this class. Slow but will almost certainly finish. Line quality set at the floor (1.0, no widening) — a full-size pickup, not built for a clean racing line. Peak-power road speed set low — a torquey turbo V6 tuned for towing, not revs.

name: Fiat Strada
notes: Fiat Strada Endurance 1.3 CS (2024+), Brazil's best-selling vehicle overall (2022-2026, 84k units in H1 2026 alone). 1.3 GSE Firefly flex 8v, 107 cv on ethanol (verified: 98 cv gasoline / 107 cv ethanol — ethanol figures used roster-wide for the Brazilian cars), 5MT, FWD, curb weight 1055 kg (verified). Manufacturer 171 km/h top speed and 11.6 s 0-100 (verified). cdA is an estimate (~0.38 Cd x ~2.5 m2) — a compact but boxy unibody pickup. Light-truck tyres on an unladen bed give the lowest grip among the Brazilian entries. Aggression set slightly high — Brazil's work-pickup fleet is famously driven flat out. Line quality at the floor — it's a work tool. Naturally aspirated (R9): loses power with altitude. Peak-power road speed set roster-typical for a small NA four.

name: VW Polo Track
notes: Volkswagen Polo Track 1.0 MPI (2023+), the volume trim behind the Polo's #1 passenger-car spot in Brazil (54k units in H1 2026). 1.0 MPI flex 12v 3-cyl, 84 cv on ethanol (verified: 77 cv gasoline / 84 cv ethanol), 5MT, FWD, curb weight 1054 kg (verified). Manufacturer 169 km/h and 13.4 s 0-100 (verified) — the least powerful car in this roster. cdA is an estimate (~0.30 Cd x ~2.05 m2) on the MQB-A0 hatch body. Standard economy tyres. Line quality slightly above floor — a tidy, well-sorted small hatch chassis. Naturally aspirated (R9): loses power with altitude. Peak-power road speed set roster-typical for a small NA three.

name: VW T-Cross
notes: Volkswagen T-Cross 200 TSI (2024 facelift), Brazil's best-selling SUV four years running (49k units in H1 2026, #3 overall). 1.0 TSI flex turbo 3-cyl, 128 cv on ethanol (verified: 116 cv gasoline / 128 cv ethanol), 6AT, FWD, curb weight 1259 kg (verified). Manufacturer ~185 km/h and 10.1 s 0-100 (verified; some sources list 192 km/h — the conservative figure used). cdA is an estimate (~0.35 Cd x ~2.35 m2) — a tall small crossover. Crossover all-season tyres, RAV4-like grip. Driven like the family car it is — low aggression, low error. Line quality at the floor — a tall crossover with no precision pretensions. Peak-power road speed set low — a torquey small turbo.

name: Fiat Argo
notes: Fiat Argo Drive 1.0 (2023+), #4 overall in Brazil H1 2026. 1.0 Firefly flex 6v 3-cyl, 75 cv on ethanol (verified: 71 cv gasoline / 75 cv ethanol), 5MT, FWD, curb weight 1074 kg (verified). Manufacturer 162 km/h on ethanol and ~13.4 s 0-100 (verified) — the slowest top speed in this roster. cdA is an estimate (~0.32 Cd x ~2.1 m2). Standard economy tyres. Line quality at the floor — a budget commuter hatch. Naturally aspirated (R9): loses power with altitude. Peak-power road speed set roster-typical for a small NA three.

name: Chevrolet Onix Turbo
notes: Chevrolet Onix 1.0 Turbo (2020+), #5 overall in Brazil H1 2026 after four years as champion (2016-2019, pre-Strada era). 1.0 turbo flex 12v 3-cyl, 116 cv on either fuel (verified), 6AT, FWD, curb weight ~1065 kg (verified). Manufacturer 187 km/h and 10.1 s 0-100 (verified) — the quickest of the Brazilian volume cars. cdA is an estimate (~0.31 Cd x ~2.1 m2) on the slippery GEM-platform hatch body. Standard economy tyres. Aggression set slightly high — the ride-hailing and highway-commuter fleet works these hard. Line quality slightly above floor. Peak-power road speed set low — a small turbo tuned for low-end torque.

name: Opala Comodoro 4.1
notes: Chevrolet Opala Comodoro 4.1 (final generation, 1988-1992) — the Brazilian classic, here in its last and best-documented form. 4.1L (4092 cm3, the 250-cid Chevrolet straight-six, popularly nicknamed '4.2'), carburetted, 121 cv net on gasoline at just 3800 rpm and 29 kgf.m at 2000 rpm (verified — pre-1987 quotes of ~171 cv are SAE gross, a different rating system), 5MT, RWD. Curb weight ~1379 kg (verified via the published 11.4 kg/cv weight-to-power ratio). Factory 169 km/h and 12 s 0-100 (verified). cdA is an estimate (~0.45 Cd x ~2.1 m2) — a boxy 1968-vintage body. Period-style narrow radials on a live rear axle: the lowest grip in the roster, and the famously tail-happy RWD chassis earns the highest errorSigma among the road cars. Aggression set high — nobody buys a 4.1 straight-six to drive it gently. Line quality at the floor: soft suspension, slow steering. Naturally aspirated (R9): loses power with altitude. Peak-power road speed set low — a low-revving torque-first straight-six.

name: Tesla Model 3 LR
notes: Tesla Model 3 Long Range AWD (2023). ~366 hp combined (third-party dyno estimate). Cd 0.23 x ~2.22 m2 - among the lowest-drag production cars. Low-rolling-resistance EV tyres. Dual-motor traction control aids longitudinal grip. 145 mph claimed top speed. Line quality set slightly above default — composed but a heavier EV, not a dedicated precision chassis. Peak-power road speed left at the floor default — EVs deliver full torque from a standstill.

name: Porsche 911
notes: Porsche 911 Carrera 992 (3.0L twin-turbo flat-6, PDK). 379 hp crank. Cd 0.29 x ~2.0 m2. Sports tyres. Rear-engine weight bias aids traction and cornering grip. Manufacturer-claimed 182 mph. Line quality set high — the archetypal precision sports car, confidence-inspiring on a chosen line. Peak-power road speed set moderate-high — a sports-tuned turbo flat-6 that likes to rev.

name: Chevrolet Corvette Z06
notes: Chevrolet Corvette Z06 (C8, 2023+), 5.5L naturally aspirated flat-plane-crank V8 (LT6), 8-speed DCT. 670 hp crank, curb weight 1662 kg (verified: GM Authority official specs). Cd 0.309 (verified) x ~2.0 m2 frontal area estimate. Extreme summer performance tyres (Michelin Pilot Sport Cup 2). Mid-engine weight distribution gives the best grip in this roster — its real cornering limit (muLat) is already the highest here, so aggression is kept at 1.0 rather than stacked on top of it. Manufacturer/chief-engineer-confirmed 195 mph top speed on standard aero (189 mph with the high-downforce Z07 package). Line quality set high — mid-engine track car with exceptional driver feedback and line precision. Naturally aspirated (R9): loses power with altitude in proportion to air density, unlike this roster's turbo/hybrid/electric cars. Peak-power road speed set high — an extremely high-revving flat-plane-crank NA V8.

name: Nissan GT-R Premium
notes: Nissan GT-R Premium (R35, 2023), 3.8L twin-turbo V6 (VR38DETT), 6-speed DCT, AWD (ATTESA E-TS). 565 hp crank (verified: Nissan press kit), curb weight 1784 kg / 3933 lb (verified) — the heaviest of the sports cars here. Cd 0.26 (verified) x ~2.16 m2 frontal area estimate, unusually low drag for the class. High-performance summer tyres. AWD launch and computer-managed torque split ('Godzilla') make it the most forgiving and predictable of the fast cars, hence the low errorSigma. Manufacturer-claimed 196 mph, electronically limited (verified). Line quality set moderately high — computer-managed AWD is forgiving but not scalpel-precise like the RWD sports cars here. Peak-power road speed set moderate — a torquey twin-turbo V6.

name: Audi R8 V10 Performance
notes: Audi R8 V10 Performance Quattro (2022, final V10 model year), 5.2L naturally aspirated V10, 7-speed DCT, AWD (quattro). 602 hp crank (verified: US-spec Audi rating), curb weight 1650 kg / 3638 lb (verified US-spec coupe). Cd 0.36 (verified) x ~2.1 m2 frontal area estimate. Performance summer tyres. AWD grip and a mid-engine layout give a wide, confidence-inspiring envelope. Manufacturer-claimed 205 mph — the highest top speed in this roster. Line quality set high — mid-engine AWD supercar with a wide, confidence-inspiring precision envelope. Naturally aspirated (R9): loses power with altitude in proportion to air density, unlike this roster's turbo/hybrid/electric cars. Peak-power road speed set high — a high-revving NA V10.

name: Ferrari 296 GTB
notes: Ferrari 296 GTB (2022+), 2.9L twin-turbo V6 plug-in hybrid + electric motor, 8-speed DCT, RWD, mid-engine. 819 hp combined SAE crank rating (verified: Ferrari/press specs), curb weight ~1620 kg (verified range 1592-1648 kg; Ferrari's own 1470 kg figure is dry weight, not curb weight). Cd 0.38 (verified) x ~2.0 m2 frontal area estimate. Extreme summer performance tyres. RWD-only, so it needs slightly more respect at the limit than the AWD cars in this class despite the mid-engine balance. Manufacturer-claimed 205 mph. Line quality set high — precision mid-engine supercar chassis. Peak-power road speed set low-moderate — turbo-hybrid, biased toward low-end torque.

name: Lamborghini Huracan EVO
notes: Lamborghini Huracan EVO AWD / LP 640-4 (2019+), 5.2L naturally aspirated V10, 7-speed DCT, AWD. 631 hp crank (verified: 640 PS), curb weight 1551 kg (verified). Cd not published by Lamborghini in available sources — cdA is an estimate (~0.36 Cd x ~2.0 m2 frontal area) consistent with the mid-engine-supercar class. Extreme summer performance tyres. AWD launch and grip make it confidence-inspiring, similar in character to the R8. Manufacturer-claimed 202 mph. Line quality set high — precision mid-engine AWD supercar, similar character to the R8. Naturally aspirated (R9): loses power with altitude in proportion to air density, unlike this roster's turbo/hybrid/electric cars. Peak-power road speed set high — a high-revving NA V10.

name: McLaren 720S
notes: McLaren 720S (2017-2023), 4.0L twin-turbo V8 (M840T), 7-speed DCT, RWD, carbon-fibre Monocage II tub. 710 hp / 720 PS / 529.5 kW crank (verified), DIN curb weight 1419 kg (verified) — the lightest car in the supercar tier here, with the best power-to-weight below the hypercars. Cd not officially published — cdA is an estimate (~0.32 Cd x ~1.94 m2 frontal area) consistent with its class-leading claimed efficiency. Pirelli P Zero Corsa extreme summer tyres. Manufacturer-claimed 212 mph / 341 km/h (verified). RWD-only with a famously lively rear end at the limit — errorSigma set slightly above the AWD supercars, like the 296 GTB it rivals. Line quality set high — a mid-engine chassis renowned for steering feel and precision. Peak-power road speed set moderate-high — big turbos but revs to 8100 rpm.

name: Lamborghini Aventador SVJ
notes: Lamborghini Aventador SVJ (2019-2021), 6.5L naturally aspirated V12, 7-speed ISR, AWD. 759 hp / 770 PS / 566 kW crank (verified). Lamborghini's 1525 kg figure is dry weight — curb weight set to ~1750 kg per independent instrumented tests (Car and Driver measured ~3868 lb). cdA is an estimate (~0.38 Cd x ~2.1 m2): the ALA active-aero system trades drag for downforce, and the SVJ runs draggier than sleeker rivals. Pirelli P Zero Trofeo R semi-slick tyres and +40% downforce over the SV — Nurburgring production-car record holder at launch (6:44.97), hence the highest cornering grip (muLat) in the roster. Manufacturer-claimed 217 mph / 350 km/h. A single-clutch V12 monster that demands commitment — errorSigma set a notch above the calmer AWD supercars. Line quality set high — record-setting track precision. Naturally aspirated (R9): loses power with altitude in proportion to air density. Peak-power road speed set high — the V12 revs to 8700 rpm.

name: Rimac Nevera
notes: Rimac Nevera (2021+, 150 units), quad-motor EV, single-speed, AWD torque vectoring, 120 kWh structural battery. 1914 PS / 1408 kW combined (verified), curb weight 2150 kg (verified) — the only car here in the Chiron's power league, and nearly as heavy. The roster-wide 0.85 crank-to-wheel factor overstates EV drivetrain loss a little (documented convention in cars.ts). cdA is an estimate (~0.30 Cd x ~2.2 m2 frontal area). Michelin Pilot Sport 4S tyres; four-motor torque vectoring gives the best launch traction in the roster (1.85 s 0-60, verified) and makes it the most computer-managed, forgiving car at speed — hence the roster-lowest errorSigma. vMax is the 352 km/h customer-car electronic limit; the 412 km/h record run (verified) required a special unlocked event. Like the Chiron, a 2.15-tonne hypercar isn't flung through tight corners — muLat and aggression kept conservative; its weapons are launch, torque-fill out of corners, and the straights. Aggression sits below even the Chiron's: unlike every other car here, its grip-limited acceleration reaches the cornering limit of a twisty approach road, and a driver leaning on that limit in a 2.15 t car has no braking margin left (empirically it repeatedly ran the first-hairpin trap on petropolis-teresopolis at aggression 0.94; 0.90 races cleanly). Peak-power road speed left at the floor default — full torque from a standstill.

name: Bugatti Chiron
notes: Bugatti Chiron (base, 2016-2023; not the 1578 hp Super Sport variant), 8.0L quad-turbo W16, 7-speed DCT, AWD. 1479 hp crank (verified: 1500 PS / 1103 kW), curb weight 2043 kg / 4504 lb (verified) — by far the heaviest and most powerful car in this roster. Cd 0.36 (verified) x ~2.4 m2 frontal area estimate (a wide car with large cooling intakes for the W16). Electronically limited to 261 mph (verified), the highest top speed here by a huge margin. A 2-tonne hypercar isn't built to be flung through tight corners the way a light sports car is — despite AWD and huge tyres, muLat/aggression are kept conservative (real-world lap times confirm the Chiron isn't class-leading in corners); its edge is straight-line speed on the open highway sections. Line quality set only slightly above the floor — a 2-tonne hypercar isn't flung through a precise line the way a light sports car is, despite AWD and huge tyres. Peak-power road speed set low — a quad-turbo W16 with monstrous low-end torque.

name: Yangwang U9 Xtreme
notes: Yangwang U9 Xtreme (BYD, 2025, 30 units) — the most powerful production car in the world: quad-motor EV, 3018 hp / 2220 kW combined (verified), ~1200V platform, motors to 30,000 rpm. Curb weight 2480 kg (verified) — heavier than even the Chiron. Holder of the outright production-car top-speed record: 496.22 km/h at Papenburg, Sept 2025 (verified), taking the crown from Bugatti — vMax uses it. cdA is an estimate (~0.40 Cd x ~2.2 m2, low-drag record trim runs cleaner but customer aero is draggier). Semi-slick track tyres and torque-vectoring give huge traction, but at 2.5 t the cornering targets stay conservative — and aggression sits at the roster floor for the same reason as the Nevera's (documented there): its grip-limited acceleration reaches cornering limits on approach roads where a heavy car has no braking margin left. Peak-power road speed at the floor — EV. The roster-wide 0.85 crank-to-wheel factor overstates EV loss a little (documented convention in cars.ts).

name: Koenigsegg Gemera
notes: Koenigsegg Gemera HV8 (production spec, 2025) — the world's most powerful hybrid and combustion-engined production car: 5.0L twin-turbo hot-V8 + Dark Matter axial-flux e-motor, 2300 hp / 1715 kW combined and 2750 Nm (verified), Light Speed Tourbillon transmission, AWD. Four seats. DIN curb weight 2040 kg (verified). Koenigsegg-stated 400 km/h top speed (verified claim). cdA is an estimate (~0.33 Cd x ~2.0 m2). Performance summer tyres on a 2-tonne grand tourer — a family hypercar, not a corner scalpel: conservative cornering targets, aggression kept low (same heavy-hypercar reasoning as the Chiron/Nevera). Turbocharged + electric ('forced'): no altitude derate. Peak-power road speed set very low — the e-motor torque-fills from idle.

name: Rimac Nevera R
notes: Rimac Nevera R (2025, 40 units) — the track-focused evolution of the base Nevera in this roster: quad-motor EV, 2107 hp / 1571 kW (verified), 2340 Nm, 108 kWh pack, curb weight ~2125 kg / 4685 lb (verified) — slightly lighter than the base car. Manufacturer-stated 256 mph / 412 km/h top speed (verified). cdA is an estimate (~0.33 Cd x ~2.1 m2 — the fixed rear wing adds drag over the base car). Michelin Cup 2R semi-slicks and retuned torque vectoring lift both grip axes above the base Nevera, but it remains a 2.1 t car: cornering targets stay conservative and aggression stays at 0.90 (see the base Nevera's note for the braking-margin trap this avoids). Peak-power road speed at the floor — EV. The roster-wide 0.85 crank-to-wheel factor overstates EV loss a little (documented convention in cars.ts).

name: Lotus Evija
notes: Lotus Evija (2023+, 130 units) — the most powerful British production car: quad-motor EV, 1500 kW / ~2012 PS (verified target rating), carbon monocoque, curb weight ~1887 kg / 4160 lb (verified) — the lightest of the 2000-hp club. Top speed electronically limited to 218 mph / 350 km/h (verified). cdA is an estimate (~0.30 Cd x ~2.0 m2 — the Venturi tunnels make it unusually slippery for the downforce it makes). Cup-class tyres, active aero and the lightest weight in this power tier justify the best cornering grip of the five hyper-EVs, and slightly higher aggression — it's a Lotus, built around the corner, not the straight. Peak-power road speed at the floor — EV. The roster-wide 0.85 crank-to-wheel factor overstates EV loss a little (documented convention in cars.ts).

name: Aspark Owl
notes: Aspark Owl (2020+, 50 units) — Japan's quad-motor EV hypercar: 1480 kW / 2012 PS (verified manufacturer rating; some sources quote 1985 hp), curb weight ~1900 kg / 4189 lb (verified), and at 99 cm tall the lowest production car in the world. Manufacturer-stated 413 km/h top speed (verified claim); 0-60 in 1.72 s. cdA is an estimate (~0.29 Cd x ~2.15 m2 — extremely low body, but wide). Performance summer tyres; the least track-proven of the 2000-hp club, hence the slightly higher errorSigma. Cornering targets conservative and aggression 0.90, same heavy-hyper-EV reasoning as the Nevera. Peak-power road speed at the floor — EV. The roster-wide 0.85 crank-to-wheel factor overstates EV loss a little (documented convention in cars.ts).
